Definition: to leave but a sixth part of; meaning uncertain
BiblicalUsage: This word stands once, in Ezekiel's oracle against Gog: I will turn thee back, and leave but the sixth part of thee, and will bring thee upon the mountains of Israel. The lexicon says to annihilate, but the verse says the opposite: God leaves a sixth part, and brings it up to be judged on the mountains.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the verse corrects the lexicon, for God does not annihilate Gog at once but leaves a part and leads it on, and I hold that His judgments are measured, not wild.
